memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the servant told Isaac all he had done. Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, and he married Rebekah. So she became his wife, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death." - Gen 24:66-67 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The long journey ends beautifully. Isaac takes Rebekah as his wife, "and he loved her." And in a tender line, we read that "Isaac was comforted after his mother's death." Sarah had died some time before, and Isaac had carried that grief. Now God brings comfort through the gift of a loving companion.

This is one of the first times the Bible speaks plainly of a husband loving his wife, and it is a lovely picture of God's design for marriage — a bond of genuine love and companionship. But notice the deeper note: God is a God who comforts the grieving. He saw Isaac's sorrow and, in His timing, brought healing.

Grief is real, and it is not quickly erased. Isaac mourned his mother. Yet God did not leave him in that sorrow forever. In His kindness, God brought new joy and comfort into Isaac's life.

If you are grieving today, hold on to this: our God sees your tears and is the God of all comfort (2 Cor 1:3-4). He may not remove the loss, but He tenderly brings healing and new mercies in His time. The One who comforted Isaac still comforts His children — and in Christ, He promises a day when He will wipe away every tear (Rev 21:4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I need God's comfort in a season of grief or loss?
2. Can I trust God to bring healing and new mercies in His time?
3. How can I be a comfort to someone who is grieving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are the God of all comfort. Meet me in my sorrows, bring healing in Your time, and thank You for the promise that one day You will wipe away every tear. Amen.
